1) D93 recognizes cryptic binding site on denatured collagen IV, 2) D93 inhibits bFGF-induced angiogenesis in CAM assay and tumor growth of human MDA-MB 435 tumors in mice, and 3) D93 inhibitory effects on tumor growth are more effective when it is combined with Taxol.
a novel humanized anti-denatured (dn)-collagen monoclonal antibody, D93, inhibits angiogenesis in vitro and in vivo and inhibits tumor growth in mice.
we have characterized a novel human monoclonal antibody that recognizes denatured collagen IV and blocks tumor growth and angiogenesis in vivo.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a novel monoclonal antibody that recognizes denatured collagen, and that antibody can be used to inhibit angiogenesis in the CAM assay, and to inhibit the growth of orthotopic tumors in mice.
the anti-collagen IV dn humanized antibody D-93 inhibits angiogenic and tumor growth in vivo.

the novel monoclonal antibody D93 recognizes cryptic epitopes in denatured collagen IV exposed on the sub-endothelial basement membranes of tumor blood vessels, and inhibits neo-vascularization and tumor growth by blocking the interaction between collagen IV and angiogenesis-associated molecules such as VEGF, bFGF, and MMPs.

the cryptic epitopes on collagen are conserved in different species, including human and chicken, and are exposed on denatured collagen, but are masked in native collagen.
